moat_against: Price-competed, broker-intermediated products — employers and brokers re-bid group coverage; no network effects and no structural pricing power beyond rate filings justified actuarially

Legacy Closed Block long-term care — 2025 reserve assumption updates added a $643.1M pre-tax LTC charge and the block still ran an adjusted operating loss in Q2 2026; reserve risk is not fully retired despite the Fortitude Re cession
Claims and rate hostage — benefit ratios ride disability incidence/recovery and morbidity experience, and investment income rides the yield curve, all outside management control

Capital intensity and regulation — insurance capital rules and ratings gate growth and capital return; much larger rivals (MetLife, Prudential, Lincoln, Aflac) carry bigger scale and technology budgets
moat_for: #1 U.S. group disability income position and #2 in voluntary benefits (Colonial Life) — specialist scale in workplace benefits built over decades

Switching costs via employer HR integration — HR Connect / Total Leave platforms embed claims, leave and benefits administration into the employer's HR stack, making carrier changes disruptive; high persistency (UK 91.8% cited in Q3 2025 reporting)
Broker and employer distribution — deep, loyal broker network across Unum US, Unum International (UK/Poland) and Colonial Life's agent force

Through-cycle core profitability — OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years; core adjusted operating returns strong (consolidated adjusted operating ROE ~15.9% in Q2 2026 per company reporting; 21.4% in Q3 2025); diluted shares shrinking 5.1%/yr on buybacks
moat_justification: Moderate/narrow insurer moat (5/10): the leading U.S. group disability franchise plus Colonial Life voluntary benefits, embedded in employer HR systems through HR Connect/Total Leave with high persistency and a deep broker network — real switching friction and specialist scale. Against: group benefits are price-competed and periodically re-bid through brokers, there are no network effects, claims experience and rates are outside management control, and the legacy Closed Block long-term care book has repeatedly produced reserve charges (FY2025 OE/share fell to $2.90 on the LTC assumption update). Return evidence: fundamentals.json carries no roic_proxy series for UNM (null every year — the filer's operating-income tagging does not produce one) and no gross margin (insurers file no COGS/gross profit), so the return anchor is ROE from fundamentals.json: 16.3% (2021), 16.1% (2022), 13.3% (2023), 16.2% (2024), then 6.6% in charge-hit 2025 — mid-teens in normal years, not the sustained >20% through-cycle record a 7+ moat would need, and GAAP ROE is repeatedly knocked down by the legacy block.
name: Unum Group
one_liner: Quality workplace-benefits insurer (U.S. group disability leader), moat 5/10 — does not clear 15% at $92.23 on the OCF-based model (weighted IRR 8.8%, IV@15% $45.93, Tier D, low confidence on sector mismatch); it would clear 15% only at ~$45.93, roughly half the price.
